public_rationale: A survey by Song, Han and Goodman, submitted to arXiv on 5 February 2026, says LLMs have shown remarkable reasoning capabilities. It also says that 'significant reasoning failures persist,' even in seemingly simple scenarios (e1). On 5 December 2025 the ARC Prize Foundation said AI reasoning systems 'still exhibit many flaws' and that new ideas are still needed (e2). The same ARC Prize analysis cites 2025 progress, including ARC-AGI-2 scores, IMO gold in math and a 100% ICPC result in coding (e3). That progress does not show reasoning had become solved or minor, so it does not meet the contradiction condition. Both sources describe reasoning failures as a major remaining limitation, which fits the plain reading of 'one of the core issues.'
limitations: 'Core issue' is qualitative; no metric ranks reasoning failures against other limitations.
Both sources are expert judgments, not a single measured threshold.
The evidence records substantial reasoning progress in 2025; the claim is qualitative and does not deny that progress.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Authoritative evaluations in this period show that reasoning had become a solved or minor issue for frontier LLMs.
